Here's what I found related to your search on Flutter's Swift Package Manager (SwiftPM) plugin validation and the associated migration work:

## Context: SwiftPM in Flutter 3.44

The symbols you're searching for (`validatePluginSupportsSwiftPackageManager`, `kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl`, `darwin_dependency_management`) relate to Flutter's tooling that warns app developers when their plugins don't yet support SwiftPM. As of the 3.44 release, Flutter uses Swift Package Manager to manage iOS and macOS native dependencies. Flutter continues to support CocoaPods in maintenance mode, however, the CocoaPods registry permanently becomes read-only on December 2, 2026.

## The validation warning behavior

The `validatePluginSupportsSwiftPackageManager` logic produces a warning message when plugins lack a `Package.swift`. The following plugins do not support Swift Package Manager for ios: - <plugin_name> This will become an error in a future version of Flutter. If your app relies on plugins that haven't adopted Swift Package Manager yet, Flutter will print a warning listing exactly which of your dependencies are unsupported. Flutter will temporarily fall back to CocoaPods for plugins that have not adopted Swift packages yet.

## Key related pull request (#178931)

The most directly relevant PR I found is **flutter/flutter #178931 — "Add Flutter as a Swift Package dependency"** by vashworth. The main purpose of this PR is to add the Flutter framework as a Swift Package dependency. As such, Xcode will now handle the copying, thinning, and codesigning of the framework and therefore the Flutter Xcode Run Scripts shouldn't. This will allow plugins to declare a dependency on the Flutter framework package and eliminate the need for the Pre-Action "prepare" script.

This PR involved generation of the FlutterFramework swift package (this will generate a Package.swift and symlink to the Flutter framework in the artifact cache) and adding the FlutterFramework as a dependency to the FlutterGeneratedPluginSwiftPackage (the Swift package the Xcode project has a dependency on). A follow-up PR (#179512) was planned to make the Flutter framework a local package override.

## The `darwin` / shared source aspect

The `darwin_dependency_management` reference relates to how plugins handle iOS and macOS shared code. When sharedDarwinSource is enabled, instead of an ios directory for iOS and a macos directory for macOS, both platforms use a shared darwin directory for all code and resources. In the SwiftPM plugin author docs, the example uses ios, replace ios with macos or darwin, as applicable.

## `kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl` destination

The docs URL constant points to Flutter's plugin author migration guide. A new requirement introduced for the 3.44 migration is notable: to add this support, add a Package.swift file and move your source files to match the standard Swift package structure. If you already migrated your plugin during the 2025 pilot, you need to complete one new step: you must add FlutterFramework as a dependency in your Package.swift file. Read the Flutter migration docs for plugin authors for full instructions.

# Test cases calling `validatePluginSupportsSwiftPackageManager`

All these live in the `validatePluginSupportsSwiftPackageManager` group and use real `Plugin` objects (except the example-app suppression tests, which use `FakePlugin` + `setUp`).

## 1. "returns warning when podspec exists but no Package.swift"

- **Invocation:** `platform: IOSPlugin.kConfigKey`, `fileSystem: fs`.
- **Assertions:** `warning` `isNotNull`; contains `"does not have Swift Package Manager support"`; contains `kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl`.

## 2. "returns null when Package.swift exists with FlutterFramework dependency"
- **Plugin:** `IOSPlugin`; writes a `Package.swift` whose dependencies include a package referencing FlutterFramework.
- **Invocation:** `platform: IOSPlugin.kConfigKey`.
- **Assertion:** `warning` `isNull`.

## 3. "returns warning when Package.swift exists without FlutterFramework dependency"
- **Plugin:** `IOSPlugin`; writes a `Package.swift` with empty `dependencies`.
- **Invocation:** `platform: IOSPlugin.kConfigKey`.
- **Assertions:** `isNotNull`; contains `"is missing a dependency on FlutterFramework"`; contains `kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl`.

## 4. "works with macOS platform"
- **Plugin:** `MacOSPlugin(name: 'test_plugin')`; creates `.../macos/test_plugin.podspec`.
- **Invocation:** `platform: MacOSPlugin.kConfigKey`.
- **Assertions:** `isNotNull`; contains `"macos"`.

## 5. "returns null when plugin does not support the platform"
- **Plugin:** only an `AndroidPlugin` platform entry.
- **Invocation:** `platform: IOSPlugin.kConfigKey`.
- **Assertion:** `warning` `isNull`.

## 6. "works with sharedDarwinSource plugins"
- **Plugin:** `IOSPlugin(..., sharedDarwinSource: true)` **and** `MacOSPlugin(..., sharedDarwinSource: true)`; creates `.../darwin/test_plugin.podspec`.
- **Invocations:** called twice — once with `IOSPlugin.kConfigKey`, once with `MacOSPlugin.kConfigKey`.
- **Assertions:** both warnings `isNotNull` and contain `"does not have Swift Package Manager support"`.

# Example-app warning suppression tests (via `setUp`)

Grouped under **"when building from a plugin example app"**. Two pubspec fixtures are defined: a plugin pubspec (`name: my_plugin`, with `flutter.plugin.platforms.ios.pluginClass`) and a non-plugin pubspec (`name: my_app`). Each test drives `DarwinDependencyManagement.setUp(...)` with a `FakePlugin` that has a podspec but no Package.swift, then asserts `testLogger.warningText` `isNot(contains(kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl))`.

The suppression conditions each test isolates:

- **"does not warn when project is not an example app"** — project directory is the default `'app_name'` (not ending in `example`), so validation is skipped.
- **"does not warn when parent pubspec is malformed"** — parent pubspec is `"invalid: yaml: content: [[["`; `directoryOverride: '/my_plugin/example'`.
- **"does not warn when parent directory has no pubspec.yaml"** — no parent pubspec created; `directoryOverride: '/my_plugin/example'`.
- **"does not warn when parent is not a Flutter plugin"** — parent pubspec is the non-plugin `my_app` pubspec (no `flutter.plugin` section).
- **"does not warn when plugin name not found in plugins list"** — parent pubspec declares `name: other_plugin` while the plugin list contains `my_plugin`, so the names don't match.

Together these confirm the warning only fires when: the project directory ends with `example`, a parseable parent `pubspec.yaml` exists, that parent is a Flutter plugin, and its name matches a plugin in the list.

      "message": "Stop prefetching Swift packages in pub get (#187113)

We were previously calling `prefetchSwiftPackagesForProject` in
`DarwinDependencyManagement`, which would be called during `flutter pub
get`. This would start the process silently and not wait for it to
complete. The original idea was so that when you added a dependency in
your IDE, it would start downloading any remote dependencies without you
needing to trigger a build. However, if 2 processes are fetching the
dependencies at the same time, this can cause one to fail.

I'm guessing that's what's happening in
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/186054#issuecomment-4537422042.

This PR removes the silent prefetch call from `flutter pub get`.
Instead, it will be called during `flutter build`/`flutter run`

Speculative fix for https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/186054.

      "message": "Use resolved implementation plugins with SwiftPM (#187097)

When you use a federated plugin, it can have a default package per
platform. However, app developers can override the default package by
adding a different package that implements the federated plugin as a
direct dependency. For example, the federated plugin
`google_maps_flutter` has `google_maps_flutter_ios` set as it's default
package for iOS. App developers can add `google_maps_flutter_sdk_10` to
their app's pubspec.yaml to override the default plugin and use
`google_maps_flutter_sdk_10` instead.

SwiftPM was not previously handling this use case. This PR fixes that.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/186770.

## Summary

I implemented the feature in `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/macos/darwin_dependency_management.dart` (source only — no test files touched):

1. **Added import** `'../flutter_manifest.dart'` (needed to parse the parent `pubspec.yaml`).

2. **`validatePluginSupportsSwiftPackageManager` static method** — takes a `Plugin`, `fileSystem`, and `platform` string, and:
   - Returns a warning containing `'does not have Swift Package Manager support'` + `kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl` when the plugin has a podspec but no `Package.swift`.
   - Returns `null` when a `Package.swift` exists and contains `'FlutterFramework'`.
   - Returns a warning containing `'is missing a dependency on FlutterFramework'` + `kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl` when `Package.swift` exists but lacks `'FlutterFramework'`.
   - Interpolates the platform name (`macos`/`ios`) into the message. Because `pluginPodspecPath`/`pluginSwiftPackageManifestPath` return `null` for unsupported platforms (and route through the `darwin` directory for `sharedDarwinSource` plugins), the method automatically returns `null` for unsupported platforms and correctly handles shared-Darwin plugins for both iOS and macOS.

3. **`kSwiftPackageManagerDocsUrl` constant** exported at file scope, set to `'https://docs.flutter.dev/packages-and-plugins/swift-package-manager/for-plugin-authors'`.

4. **`setUp` integration** — added a call to a new private `_validateExampleAppPluginSupportsSwiftPackageManager` after analytics are sent. Its helper `_loadPluginFromExampleProject` suppresses the warning unless every condition holds: the project directory ends with `example`, the parent `pubspec.yaml` exists, parses successfully, declares a Flutter plugin, and its name matches a plugin in the known plugin list.

`dart analyze` reports no issues.

Sources: [flutter/flutter PR #182246](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/182246), [Swift Package Manager for plugin authors](https://docs.flutter.dev/packages-and-plugins/swift-package-manager/for-plugin-authors)
